explanation: Herodotus recorded an Egyptian story that a phoenix visited Heliopolis once every 500 years, but admitted he had seen one only in paintings.

claims.text: In legend, the phoenix is reborn from its own ashes.
The griffin, the roc and the thunderbird are not said to be reborn from their own ashes.
Herodotus recorded that, according to the people of Heliopolis in Egypt, the phoenix came there once every 500 years.
Herodotus wrote that he had seen the phoenix only in paintings.

evidence.restatement: The phoenix is the legendary bird that rises renewed from its own ashes.
No rebirth-from-ashes legend attaches to the griffin, the roc or the thunderbird.
In Histories 2.73 Herodotus reports the Heliopolitans' story that the phoenix comes to Egypt once every 500 years.

evidence.restatement: The griffin is a lion-eagle hybrid, the roc a giant bird of prey in Arabian tales and the thunderbird a Native American spirit; none has a rebirth-from-ashes story.
Herodotus (Histories 2.73) reports the Heliopolitans saying that the phoenix comes to Egypt once every five hundred years, when its father dies.
